answer: `SB_SEARCH_DIR` keeps the index on disk. Set it to a writable folder outside your space, and without it the full-text index stays in memory and is rebuilt on every start.
block:
Memory for: Which environment variable keeps the server's full-text search index on disk so it isn't rebuilt every start?
[1] Search.md (Segments)
  Single-space servers: Set `SB_SEARCH_DIR` to a writable folder outside your space to persist search indexes. Without it, full-text search runs in memory and rebuilds on startup. To enable semantic search, also set `SB_SEARCH_MODEL` to one of the model IDs above. Model files are stored in the search directory. Restart the server after changing these environment variables. See [[Install/Configuration]].
  The search index: The server keeps a full-text index of the space and updates it as pages change, usually within a second. After the server starts, it builds or catches up the index in the background. Until that finishes, results come with a “Search index building” notice and may be incomplete. / Where the index lives: / * On a server with several spaces, under `search/indexes/` in the server’s data folder, so restarts reuse it. / * On a single-space server, in memory and rebuilt at every start, or in `SB_SEARCH_DIR` when it is set (see [[#Single-space servers]]). / * In SilverBullet Desktop, in the app’s data folder.
  - The server keeps a full-text index of the space and updates it as pages change, usually within a second.
[2] CHANGELOG.md (CHANGELOG)
  2.12.1: * Each user of a space keeps one browser profile, reused after a stop or a server restart, so the client no longer rebuilds its index from scratch every time. Profiles left behind by earlier versions are deleted at startup. / * The headless client no longer focuses its editor, which cuts its idle CPU use by about three quarters. / * Fix: the [[Runtime API]] returns JSON for query rows, null values, dates and other Lua values without serialization crashes, and remains usable after the client reloads its UI. / * SLIQ errors offer more specific explanations for common mistakes.
[3] Install/Configuration.md (Network)
  - SB_SEARCH_DIR is a writable folder outside the space where search keeps its full-text index, and when unset the index is kept in memory.
  Run mode: * `SB_READ_ONLY` *(legacy)*: If you want to run the SilverBullet client and server in read-only mode (you get the full SilverBullet client, but all edit functionality and commands are disabled), you can do this by setting this environment variable to a non-empty value. Upon the server start a full space index will happen, after which all write operations will be disabled. Prefer the per-space settings in the [[Dashboard]]: give the public read access to publish a space (see [[Publishing]]), or **Freeze this space** to stop all writes.
[4] Architecture/Server.md (Server services)
  - Search maintains a server-side full-text index and, when configured, a semantic index.
[5] Architecture.md (Top-level Architecture)
  - The Server's search index supports full-text and semantic search.
Exact facts:
- [1] Search searches the text of every page in your space. Open it from the command palette or press `Ctrl-Shift-f` (`Cmd-Shift-f` on macOS). Each result shows the page name and an excerpt with the matching words highlighted.
- [1] When enabled (default off), SilverBullet offers semantic search — search based on meaning. It runs an embedding model on the server itself (in Desktop, on your computer). - [1] 2. To keep a space on full-text search only, open its settings, go to **Search** and uncheck **Semantic search**.
